propositions.name: luminiferous_ether_exists
propositions.statement: There is a luminiferous ether between the earth and light, relative to which the earth may have motion.
propositions.quote: if there be any relative motion between the earth and the luminiferous ether, it must be small; quite small enough entirely to refute Fresnel's explanation of aberration

propositions.name: ether_at_rest_or_in_motion
propositions.statement: The ether at the earth's surface is either at rest with regard to the earth or has some relative velocity with respect to it.
propositions.quote: Stokes has given a theory of aberration which assumes the ether at the earth's surface to be at rest with regard to the latter, and only requires in addition that the relative velocity have a potential

propositions.name: light_velocity_in_stationary_ether
propositions.statement: V is the velocity of light in the ether supposed stationary.
propositions.quote: Let V be the velocity of light in the ether supposed stationary, and let cd be the increase in the distance the light has to travel to reach d .

propositions.name: earth_moves_through_ether
propositions.statement: The earth has a motion through the ether, and the effect of this motion on the path of a ray can be considered.
propositions.quote: In deducing the formula for the quantity to be measured, the effect of the motion of the earth through the ether on the path of the ray at right angles to this motion was overlooked.

propositions.name: apparatus_moves_through_resting_ether
propositions.statement: When the ether is at rest and the whole apparatus moves in the direction sc with the velocity of the earth, the directions and distances traversed by the rays are altered.
propositions.quote: Suppose now, the ether being at rest, that the whole apparatus moves in the direction sc , with the velocity of the earth in its orbit, the directions and distances traversed by the rays will be altered thus

propositions.name: transit_time_well_defined
propositions.statement: T is the time light occupies to pass from a to c and is a single quantity used in the calculation.
propositions.quote:
T=time light occupies to pass from a to c . 
 T =time light occupies to return from c to a / , (fig. 2.)

propositions.name: second_order_offset_does_not_matter
propositions.statement: The two returning rays not meeting exactly at the same point, the difference being of the second order, does not affect the validity of the reasoning.
propositions.quote: It may be remarked that the rays ba / and ca / , do not now meet exactly in the same point a / , though the difference is of the second order; this does not affect the validity of the reasoning.

propositions.name: rotation_reverses_path_difference
propositions.statement: When the whole apparatus is turned through 90°, the path difference is in the opposite direction, so the displacement of the interference fringes should double.
propositions.quote: If now the whole apparatus be turned through 90°, the difference will be in the opposite direction, hence the displacement of the interference fringes should be

propositions.name: path_difference_causes_fringe_shift
propositions.statement: A difference between the two paths produces a displacement of the interference fringes that is proportional to the difference.
propositions.quote:
if there is any displacement
due to the relative motion of the earth and the luminiferous ether, this cannot be much greater than 0.01 of the distance between the fringes.

propositions.name: arms_equal_in_apparatus
propositions.statement: The distances ab and ac are equal in the apparatus, both of length D.
propositions.quote: The paths being now approximately equal, the two images of the source of light or of some well-defined object placed in front of the condensing lens, were made to coincide

propositions.name: perpendicular_path_length_formula
propositions.statement: The length of the path of the ray at right angles to the motion has a term in v squared over V squared and is treated by the same degree of accuracy as the other path.
propositions.quote: In deducing the formula for the quantity to be measured, the effect of the motion of the earth through the ether on the path of the ray at right angles to this motion was overlooked.

propositions.name: rigid_apparatus_under_rotation
propositions.statement: The apparatus can be revolved without producing distortion in the geometry of the paths.
propositions.quote: In the first experiment one of the principal difficulties encountered was that of revolving the apparatus without producing distortion; and another was its extreme sensitiveness to vibration.

propositions.name: wooden_rod_measures_optical_path
propositions.statement: The lengths of the two optical paths can be measured by a light wooden rod reaching diagonally from mirror to mirror.
propositions.quote: the lengths of the two paths were measured by a light wooden rod reaching diagonally from mirror to mirror, the distance being read from a small steel scale to tenths of millimeters.

propositions.name: two_equal_paths_interfere
propositions.statement: When the paths ab and ac are equal, the two rays interfere along ad.
propositions.quote: If then the paths ab and ac are equal, the two rays interfere along ad .

propositions.name: aberration_tangent_equals_ratio
propositions.statement: The tangent of the angle of aberration is the ratio of the velocity of the earth to the velocity of light.
propositions.quote: if the tangent of the angle of aberration is the ratio of the velocity of the earth to the velocity of light, then, since the latter velocity in water is three-fourths its velocity in a vacuum

propositions.name: water_reduces_light_velocity
propositions.statement: The velocity of light in water is three-fourths its velocity in a vacuum, so the aberration observed with a water telescope should be four-thirds of its true value.
propositions.quote: since the latter velocity in water is three-fourths its velocity in a vacuum, the aberration observed with a water telescope should be four-thirds of its true value.

propositions.name: fresnel_partial_ether_drag
propositions.statement: The ether in the interior of a transparent medium is supposed to move with a velocity less than the velocity of the medium in the ratio (n²-1)/n².
propositions.quote: the ether is supposed to be at rest except in the interior of transparent media , in which secondly, it is supposed to move with a velocity less than the velocity of the medium in the ratio

propositions.name: ether_passes_through_metals
propositions.statement: The ether can and does pass through metals, though we cannot assume opaque bodies offer free passage.
propositions.quote: But there can hardly be question that the ether can and does pass through metals. Lorentz cites the illustration of a metallic barometer tube .

propositions.name: ether_imcompressible
propositions.statement: The ether is imcompressible, so when a tube is inclined the ether above the mercury is forced out.
propositions.quote: When the tube is inclined the ether in the space above the mercury is certainly forced out, for it is imcompressible.

propositions.name: noon_evening_observations_comparable
propositions.statement: Observations made near noon and observations made near six o'clock in the evening are means of six readings that are expressed graphically for comparison.
propositions.quote: The following tables give the means of the six readings ; the first, for observations made near noon, the second, those near six o'clock in the evening.

propositions.name: orbital_motion_is_motion_through_ether
propositions.statement: The motion of the earth in its orbit gives the displacement to be expected, so orbital motion is treated as motion through the ether.
propositions.quote: Considering only the velocity of the earth in its orbit, this would be

propositions.name: solar_motion_combines_with_orbital
propositions.statement: The orbital motion of the earth may be combined with the motion of the solar system to yield a resultant velocity through the ether.
propositions.quote: If this is combined with the motion of the solar system, concerning which but little is known with certainty, the result would have to be modified

propositions.name: displacement_proportional_to_square_velocity
propositions.statement: The displacement of the fringes is proportional to the square of the velocity of the earth relative to the ether.
propositions.quote: But since the displacement is proportional to the square of the velocity, the relative velocity of the earth and the ether is probably less than one sixth the earth's orbital velocity, and certainly less than one-fourth.

propositions.name: first_power_measurable_in_principle
propositions.statement: The first power of the relative velocity of the earth with respect to the ether could be measured, if the velocity of light could be measured without returning the ray to its starting point.
propositions.quote: If it were possible to measure with sufficient accuracy the velocity of light without returning the ray to its starting point, the problem of measuring the first power of the relative velocity of the earth

propositions.name: jupiter_eclipses_measure_ether_velocity
propositions.statement: Observations of the eclipses of Jupiter's satellites can give the motion of the solar system with reference to the luminiferous ether itself.
propositions.quote: will give, not merely the motion of the solar system with reference to the stars, but with reference to the luminiferous ether itself.

propositions.name: mercury_float_permits_free_rotation
propositions.statement: Mounting the apparatus on a massive stone floating on mercury overcomes the difficulty of revolving the apparatus without producing distortion.
propositions.quote: The first named difficulties were entirely overcome by mounting the apparatus on a massive stone floating on mercury; and the second by increasing, by repeated reflection, the path of the light to about ten times its former value.

propositions.name: repeated_reflection_multiplies_shift
propositions.statement: Increasing by repeated reflection the path of the light to ten times its former value multiplies the expected fringe displacement by the same factor.
propositions.quote: the second by increasing, by repeated reflection, the path of the light to about ten times its former value.

propositions.name: sixteen_marks_give_direction_reference
propositions.statement: The sixteen equidistant marks around the cast-iron trough serve as reference positions relative to which the changing direction of motion through the ether is recorded.
propositions.quote: The observations were conducted as follows: Around the cast-iron trough were sixteen equidistant marks. The apparatus was revolved very slowly (one turn in six minutes)

propositions.name: uniform_slow_rotation_avoids_strain
propositions.statement: Keeping the apparatus in slow uniform motion gives more uniform and consistent results, as the effects of strains and change of temperature would otherwise come into action.
propositions.quote: for the effects of strains could be noted for at least half a minute after the stone came to rest, and during this time effects of change of temperature came into action.

propositions.name: resultant_velocity_at_observation_meaningful
propositions.statement: There is a resultant velocity of the earth through the ether at the time of the observations, and repeating the experiment at intervals of three months removes the chance that this resultant is small.
propositions.quote: and it is just possible that the resultant velocity at the time of the observations was small though the chances are much against it. The experiment will therefore be repeated at intervals of three months, and thus all uncertainty will be avoided.
